subject.title: feat(feeds): add publisher following control UI

question: Should OpenClaw core permanently own signed publisher following through gateway RPCs, a top-level CLI, shared SQLite state, an automatic network scheduler, and the Control UI before the linked RFC and ClawHub contract are accepted?
rationale: The patch is not merely UI plumbing; it establishes a new persisted and security-sensitive product contract whose permanent owner and compatibility obligations require explicit maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor and harden the core stack
options.body: Approve core ownership, then require the profile-independent removal fix, bottom-up stack landing, upgrade checks, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Wait for contract approval
options.body: Keep the draft parked until the linked RFC and ClawHub feed contract establish the protocol and trust model.

options.title: Narrow to UI after RPC approval
options.body: Split this PR back to the Control UI layer after the gateway and storage stack is independently accepted and merged.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and harden the core stack
recommendation.body: Approve core ownership, then require the profile-independent removal fix, bottom-up stack landing, upgrade checks, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans core product scope, gateway protocol, persisted state, security boundaries, and user-facing navigation rather than one isolated implementation file.
